newsitem.title: UK: Trading sparse on bourses, FTSE hits new high.
newsitem.headline: Trading sparse on bourses, FTSE hits new high.

text.p: London's blue chip FTSE stock index on Friday managed to slip above its previous peak but equity and currency trading throughout Europe was extremely light after the Christmas break.
Paris was down on profit-taking prompted by worries about Wall Street while in Frankfurt bulls were still dominant and leading shares climbed more than half a percent in early electronic trading.
London's rise to a fresh record, though small in percentage terms, was bolstered by firm bonds and a further advance on Wall Street overnight.
At 1000 GMT, the FTSE 100 was 10.1 points higher at 4,102.6, up slightly from its previous record intraday high of 4,100 set last Friday.

However, in London as with several other bourses, many dealers appeared to be extending their two-day Christmas break into the weekend and analysts said index movements were exaggerated because of the thin volumes. London Trading was closing at 1230 GMT on Friday.
In Paris, French shares slipped slightly at the opening and gave up the 2,300 level in early exchanges.

Traders said the decline was due to profit-taking prompted by some worries about Wall Street, which nearly reached a fresh record close overnight. Some dealers were expecting a further rise on Friday but others warned that the market was already overvalued.
Francois Chevallier, chief economist at bank Credit National-BFCE, told the La Tribune newspaper the Dow Jones Industrial index was 20 percent overvalued and a sharp correction lay in store for 1997.
In Frankfurt the Dax index reopened after the Christmas break nearly half a percentage point higher in a market still driven by the bulls despite some pre-holiday consolidation.
Dealers said the strength of the dollar against the mark, which makes German exports more attractive, was one factor lifting sentiment.
Trading was thin however and dealers reckoned one half or two thirds of market players were still on holiday.

In foreign exchange the dollar was stable in extremely quiet European trading. It had climbed to its highest level in more than 3-1/2 years against the yen overnight as the Japanese currency took a beating after stock prices tumbled again in Tokyo.
The dollar had been boosted by strength in stock markets at home, where the Dow Jones industrial average rose on Boxing Day for the seventh consecutive session but ended just short of a record high.
Dealers said U.S. durable goods and weekly jobless claims, due at 1330 GMT, may provide some interest.
In other currency developments, the Swiss franc continued to suffer at the hands of the mark, renewing its three-year lows at 86.41 centimes against a previous 86.20.
Sterling was steady with few fresh factors to influence sentiment and was trading at around $1.6750, little changed from around $1.6735 in European trade on Thursday.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5540 marks and 115.08 yen compared with Tuesday's closing levels of 1.5560 marks and 114.45 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 10.1 points at 4,102.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share was down 4.01 points at 2,299.74.
In Frankfurt the 30-share DAX index was up 8.55 points at 2,854.12.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $369.65 compared with its London close on Tuesday of $368.65. Silver was $4.89.
